title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator-metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, v5.0) judged every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed = 1729, resamples = 10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, precise execution accounting (model_calls_used = 200, maximum_model_calls = 400), representative validator-trace excerpts, quantitative analysis, diagnostic interpretation of the degenerate outcome, and artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up preregistered experiments (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) required to estimate validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction:
Automating NetOps workflows with generative models promises operational efficiency but raises safety and correctness concerns: a wrong or silently accepted configuration can cause outages, security exposures, or prolonged troubleshooting. A widely proposed operational pattern is generate–verify–repair (GVR): an LLM proposes a candidate configuration, a deterministic validator mechanically checks compliance with workflow policies and intent constraints, and a repair module is invoked when the validator detects a defect. Prior systems and surveys motivate verifier insertion but do not provide standardized, preregistered measurements of validator coverage (false-positive and false-negative rates), detection latency, or the end-to-end utility of repairs in operationally realistic scenarios.

We preregistered AC-2026-03 to measure whether a multidimensional validator metric suite explains more end-to-end task-success variance than a single verifier pass rate in a controlled, paired design. The design used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics: exactly one generated candidate per task was sampled and reused for both baseline (no repair) and guarded (validator+repair permitted) conditions. This isolates downstream validator/repair effects because any paired difference can only arise after the shared initial candidate is observed. Our principal contribution is an artifact-archived, preregistered execution and a candid report of a degenerate outcome (ceiling success) together with concrete, artifact-grounded prescriptions—fully implementable with the archived adapter—for follow-up confirmatory arms that can produce estimable validator FP/FN and repair utility.
sections.related_work: Architectural and prototype work across code generation, AIOps, and NetOps motivates GVR-style pipelines that interpose deterministic checks between stochastic generators and action acceptance. Cadenas [1] advocates generate–verify–repair for deterministic validation in regulated code-generation workflows; several recent NetOps/AIOps system papers and surveys document prototype deployments, benchmarks, and tool-augmented orchestrators that reduce silent failures when a validator has suitable coverage [2],[3],[4],[5]. These records show that verifier layers can detect mechanically checkable defects (compilation errors, explicit policy violations) and that benchmarked agentic systems suffer wrong-but-plausible outputs and ticket-noise sensitivity. However, the supplied literature does not deliver a standardized validator-metric suite tailored to NetOps GVR flows nor broad cross-validator empirical coverage estimates. We therefore treat prior works as architectural motivation and place our preregistered measurement experiment as an initial, rigorously archived attempt to quantify validator utility under tightly controlled semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as AC-2026-03. Key preregistered elements (archived manifest): adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model_scope = gpt-5-mini; task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count = 400); generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; independent_condition_generation = false. The primary estimand was paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the confirmatory test was an exact two-sided McNemar with paired bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistered power plan targeted detecting an absolute paired improvement of 10 percentage points at α = 0.05 with ~80% power under conservative baseline assumptions; the manifest also specified sensitivity analyses and bootstrap stability checks.

Task generation and constraints. Tasks were deterministically drawn from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task_family = intent_configuration_repair_v1) with difficulty labels 'very_hard' and 'extreme'. Each task payload in task_manifest.jsonl encodes: an initial_state, required_command_sequence, expected_final_state, allowed_fields and allowed_touched_fields, and workflow_policies (e.g., minimum_active_in_groups, must_be_down_for_fields). These constraints make each episode a mechanistically checkable intent→configuration mapping. The preregistration specified deterministic contamination checks (SHA-256 duplicate exclusion and embedding cosine similarity > 0.95) and deterministic replacement indices; the execution's contamination_summary.csv was empty (no exclusions).

Model, sampling, and adapter semantics. The declared model in execution/model_configuration.json is gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version="gpt-5-mini"). The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 200 and maximum_model_calls = 400 (one shared initial generation per pair was executed). Crucial artifact-grounded detail: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (temperature = null/unset). Null/unset does not constitute evidence of deterministic hosted-model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; provider-side sampling semantics are recorded in the adapter's provider-call audit. The adapter's audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with exactly one shared generation per task.

Validator, scoring rule, and permitted repair. Validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator emits mechanistic fields per episode: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and repair traces when repairs occur. The preregistered binary scoring rule (full_intent_constraint_validation) maps validator.valid to episode success for the primary estimand. Pipelines permitted at most one repair call per rejected candidate; repairs would toggle repair_applied and be archived in repair_provider_trace fields. The manifest enforces maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries) and complete-pair primary analysis with predefined sensitivity rules for missingness.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and audit. The adapter completed the preregistered run without technical failures: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. The execution bundle paths and representative artifact hashes (for reproducibility) include: execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256 = 23f4cd010f3a7419eb21ef9b8caf4dbe7730552eaa3f3eaa22d2068cf3b5d4e3) and execution/model_configuration.json (sha256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The preregistration manifest hash is de37b485421cb0895a98df38b6b3baad1dc7c13c81065e3d8240d2a94a0ff844.

Primary confirmatory outcome. The deterministic validator judged every sampled shared initial candidate valid and applied no repairs. Analysis artifacts record baseline_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0) and guarded_success_count = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. The paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline = 0.00; exact McNemar two-sided p-value = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. All numeric results and analysis logs are archived (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) and match these reported values.

Representative artifact diagnostics. A compact exemplar from execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json (pair-000004) illustrates validator output fields verbatim: normalized_configuration = "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"; parsed_command_count = 4; required_command_count = 4; observed_touched_field_count = 3; valid = true; repair_applied = false; validator_version = 5.0. Equivalent validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and repair_applied = false hold for every archived episode. The execution bundle therefore contains full per-episode traces but no repair artifacts because repair_applied was never set.

Exploratory diagnostics. Per-validator FP/FN estimates and repair-latency distributions are degenerate in this execution (no observed false positives, false negatives, or repairs). Missingness_summary.csv confirms complete_pair_count = 200, with zero incomplete or failed episodes. Contamination_summary.csv is empty. These artifacts permit reproducible reanalysis under alternative scoring rules or using injected faults (see Discussion prescriptions) without modifying the core archived raw responses.
sections.discussion:
Why the ceiling occurred. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics each pair re-used the identical generated candidate so any paired improvement could only arise from validator-triggered repair. The observed ceiling stems from three artifact-grounded causes visible in the archive: (1) the deterministic task generator produced reference-driven candidates that satisfied the mechanistic checks encoded in deterministic_netops_validator_v5 for the fixed generator seeds used; (2) the single-sample-per-task sampling regime removed generator variability as a source of discordance; (3) the validator enforces structural/intent-constraint checks but cannot detect all semantic intent misalignments (correct-by-structure yet incorrect-by-intent) absent an explicit intent model or operator feedback. Together these factors left no mechanical defects for the validator to detect, so no repairs could be exercised and the primary estimator had zero variance.

Implications for measurement designs. The paired shared_initial_candidate design remains appropriate to isolate validator-triggered repair effects, but it concentrates the risk that a single favorable sample will produce a ceiling. To measure validator coverage and repair utility one must (artifact-grounded) increase baseline failure prevalence or reintroduce generator variability. The archived adapter and task manifests directly support three preregisterable follow-up arms without ad hoc changes: (A) a deterministic fault-injection arm that flips a controlled fraction f of reference answers to include syntactic or configuration-logic faults (this creates measurable baseline invalidity and deterministically observable repair opportunities); (B) multi-sample stochastic generation (initial_generation_calls_per_task = k ≥ 3 independent draws) so that some draws fail validator checks and the guarded pipeline can accept or repair alternatives; (C) multi-validator comparisons and additional model families to assess external validity and sensitivity to validator implementation choices. Each prescription is implementable using the archived deterministic replacement and contamination rules recorded in the execution manifest.

Threats to validity and scope. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics were intentionally chosen to isolate downstream effects but introduced single-sample ceiling risk. Construct validity: the binary valid flag measures mechanistic, deterministic intent-constraint satisfaction but does not capture semantic alignment with operator intent. External validity: the experiment used a synthetic task bank, a single model (gpt-5-mini), and one deterministic validator; generalization to diverse production networks, multi-vendor devices, and noisy human tickets is limited. Conclusion validity: because the primary estimand exhibited zero variance, no inferential claim about repair benefit can be drawn from this execution. These limitations are recorded in the analysis artifacts and guide the artifact-grounded follow-up arms we recommend.

Operational implications and next steps. The artifact-grounded ceiling does not imply validators are unnecessary; instead it highlights that measurement of validator utility requires an execution regime that exposes realistic failure modes. Practically, operators and researchers should (1) add controlled fault-injection or curated adversarial cases to benchmark suites before evaluating repair utility; (2) preserve deterministic reproducibility by recording generation seeds and provider-call audits when increasing sampling variability; and (3) compare multiple validators on identical sampled candidates to estimate coverage differences. The execution bundle already provides the logging, contamination controls, and task-replacement primitives necessary to implement these steps reproducibly.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR pipelines. For the synthetic task bank, the sampled gpt-5-mini seeds, and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 used here, every sampled initial candidate passed the validator's mechanistic checks so no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10-percentage-point improvement) were invalidated by this ceiling outcome. All artifacts—raw responses, validator traces, execution manifests, and analysis logs—are archived to permit reproducible reanalysis. We provide concrete, artifact-grounded, preregisterable follow-up arms (fault injection, multi-sample generation, multi-validator comparison) that will produce non-degenerate data suitable for estimating validator false-positive/false-negative rates, detection latency, and repair utility in operationally meaningful conditions. These follow-up experiments are required before asserting general effectiveness of verifier-guided GVR pipelines in diverse NetOps environments.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate per pair; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not from independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
